profile.entities: Gravita India Limited; Rashtriya Metal Industries Limited (RML)

deepdive.sec: Metals Recycling & Circular Economy / Lead, Copper & EV Battery Recycling

bull_bear.body: 100% internally funded capex; working capital debt expected ₹700-900cr (metal-backed, hedged); no dividends or buybacks mentioned; focus on recycling verticals over shareholder returns
bull_bear.title: Capital allocation

bull_bear.body: West Asia logistics disruption (10-12% of sales); MCX aluminum hedging delay (impacting Al growth); copper import supply chain risks; integration execution risk with RML; regulatory delays in EPR compliance; commodity price volatility
bull_bear.title: Risks & watch-items

bull_bear.body: Confident, strategic, and execution-focused; emphasized disciplined capex, backward integration, and long-term CAGR targets; acknowledged near-term headwinds (West Asia, hedging) but framed them as temporary; tone bullish on copper and EV recycling as structural growth drivers
bull_bear.title: Management quality / tone

bull_bear.body: Copper EBITDA/ton target of ₹65,000 implies >40% margin expansion from RML’s current ₹45,000 — driven by scrap sourcing synergy and value-added product mix, not just recycling; working capital debt is treated as ‘hedged metal inventory’ not traditional debt — a key accounting nuance; aluminum/plastic margins are intentionally suppressed until MCX hedging enables scale — a deliberate capital preservation strategy
bull_bear.title: Non-obvious takeaways

bull_bear.body:
- The company reinvests profits into capacity expansion and technology upgrades.
- It maintains a conservative balance sheet with a focus on organic growth.
bull_bear.title: Capital allocation policy (investor deck)

business.body: Lead: 48,889 tons sold (+7% YoY), EBITDA/ton ₹23,043; Copper: RML acquired (31,200 tons capacity), EBITDA/ton ₹45,000, targeting ₹60,000-65,000 post-backward integration; Lithium-ion: 6,000 tons/year pilot commissioned (Jan’26); Aluminum: EBITDA/ton ₹16,043 (sustainable target ₹14,000-15,000), growth delayed pending MCX hedging; Plastic: EBITDA/ton ₹12,328 (sustainable ₹10,000-12,000); Rubber: 30,000 tons/year capacity planned (H1FY27), EBITDA/ton ₹7,000-8,000
business.title: Segment / subsidiary detail

business.body:
- The company is positioned as a leading recycling player in India, focusing on lead, aluminum, and plastics.
- It emphasizes its integrated operations from collection to manufacturing of finished products.
business.title: Positioning (investor deck)

latest_quarter.body: revenue: +10% YoY (FY26: ₹4,265cr); EBITDA/margin: +12% YoY, 10.6% margin (FY26); PAT (rptd): +21% YoY (₹378.8cr); PAT (normalized): +21% YoY (no major one-offs); order book: not disclosed; net debt: ₹118cr (pre-copper), expected to rise to ₹700-800cr post-copper capex and working capital build
latest_quarter.title: Financial scorecard

latest_quarter.body: Lead: ₹19,000-20,000/ton sustainable (Q4 pressured by West Asia); Copper: ₹45,000/ton (RML), targeting ₹60,000-65,000 with recycling integration; Aluminum: ₹14,000-15,000/ton (current ₹16,043 due to price surge); Plastic: ₹10,000-12,000/ton; Rubber: ₹7,000-8,000/ton; Cost headwinds: elevated logistics from West Asia disruption, copper import costs
latest_quarter.title: Margins & cost dynamics

outlook.body: revenue growth: 20-25% CAGR volume through FY29; margin: copper EBITDA/ton to rise from ₹45k to ₹60-65k; order inflow: not specified; capex/commissioning: ₹1,700cr total through FY29 (₹700cr copper, ₹160cr Mandvi copper recycling, ₹14cr Li-ion pilot, ₹49cr Mundra lead expansion); commissioning: copper recycling (Mandvi) in 12 months, Li-ion scaling in FY27, lead expansion (Jaipur) in Q1FY27
outlook.title: Guidance

outlook.body: Copper recycling (100,000 tons by FY29); Lithium-ion scaling; Rubber recycling (India + Romania); Steel recycling (long-term, post FY29); Value-added alloy expansion via RML
outlook.title: Growth verticals / optionality

deepdive.thesis: Gravita significantly expanded its footprint beyond lead with the RML acquisition and copper recycling capex, driving a structural shift toward higher-margin value-added copper and EV battery recycling; despite Q4 EBITDA pressure from West Asia logistics and aluminum/plastic hedging delays, the company is on track for 20-25% volume CAGR through FY29 with 20%+ ROCE expected from integrated copper operations.

open.item: Management admitted delays in capacity expansion (installed capacity still ~3.40 lakh MTPA) due to state-government consent-to-operate delays in Gujarat, expected resolved this quarter (Jan/Feb).
Mundra lead expansion of 80,000 MTPA and Jaipur lead expansion up to 45,000 MTPA both targeted for completion by Q4 FY26 (total 125,000 tons).
Applied to LME, expecting license in Q4 FY26; exploring future entry into copper, zinc, nickel and solar-panel recycling.
FY26 capex done ~INR125 crores in 9M; expected to cross INR200 crores by Q4, meeting FY26 target.
Lithium-ion plant not yet functional; consent to operate expected in next couple of days, likely functional this quarter.
Plastic volumes expected to show growth by end of FY26 as new products stabilize; EBITDA steady at ~INR10/kg.
Effective tax rate guided ~15-16% for FY26 (with treasury income), reverting to 13-14% once treasury cash deployed.
Adding ~100,000 metric tons capacity in FY26 (of which ~50,000-60,000 tons in lead), coming Q3/Q4; company 100% confident of execution.
FY26 volume growth guided ~20-25% (15-16% from existing capacity, 7-8% from new capacity coming Q3/Q4); overall 22-28% range.
Sustainable lead EBITDA guided at INR18-19 per kg with ~INR0.25-0.50 improvement per year; FY25 was ~INR20/kg due to arbitrage.
Aluminium EBITDA guided ~INR14-15 per kg and plastic ~INR10-11 per kg going forward.
FY26 volume/capacity growth guided in line with ~25% (range 20-30%); planning ~25-30% YoY capacity increase for next 3 years.
Total rubber capacity of ~60,000 MTPA to come this year (part H1, part H2); India rubber plant in H1 FY26.
Rubber (mainly Romania) revenue expected close to INR100-125 crores; ~70% CAGR growth in rubber products sold to third parties over next 3-4 years.
Aluminium MCX ADC12 approval still pending after ~1 year; contract made but not released; India aluminium scale-up held until hedging live, possibly Q1 FY27.
Jaipur (Phagi) lead capacity of ~45,000 tons to be commissioned in Q1 FY27, capacities installed, awaiting government approval.
West Asia/Middle East conflict (~10-12% of sales, mostly value-added) disrupted VAP sales and raised logistics costs, pressuring Q1 FY27 EBITDA to lower end of guidance.
Aluminium MCX listing expected by Q1 FY27 (business call of MCX; regulation complete); EPR/BWMR amendments and collection SOP expected by April 1, 2026.
India rubber capacity of ~30,000 tons to come up in H1 FY27 (Q1/Q2), Phase 1; further expansion in Mundra and Romania planned.
125,000 tons of lead capacity to be commissioned by Q4 FY26, with major incremental volumes from Q1/Q2 FY27, fully ramped by Q2 FY27.
